about: What each box of the fleet draws at the wall: the model tools/power.py and the planner read. Watts at the wall = (rest + CPU idle + CPU use x (CPU full - CPU idle) + GPU) / supply efficiency. The CPU's use and the GPU's draw are measured each five minutes; everything else here is an estimate from the parts' published power and is said to be one. Edit a box's numbers here when a meter says otherwise.
rate_about: The US average residential price of 2025, about 17 cents a kWh: a guess until Paul sets his own (Settings, Long run, power_usd_kwh).

gold.about: 80 PLUS Gold at 115 V: at least 87% efficient at 20% of its rating, 90% at 50%, 87% at 100%. A fleet box runs between, so 0.88.

saskatchewan.why: Intel rates it 65 W base and 219 W turbo; a board that lifts the limits runs all cores near 150-200 W, one that keeps them runs 65 W. 150 W until its counter is read. The rest: board, 64 GB, NVMe, fans, and an NVIDIA card with no driver loaded.

boburner.why: AMD rates it 65 W, and its package limit (PPT) is 88 W, which all cores reach under load; its I/O die idles near 20 W. The GPU is measured.

columbia.why: Intel rates it 7 W; it bursts higher. A mini PC: the rest is a few watts, and its supply an external brick.

calber.why: Intel rates it 65 W; boards let all eight cores run past it, about 95 W. The GPU is measured.

whitewolf.why: Intel rates it 91 W and it draws about that with all cores busy. The GPU is measured.

jaguaribe.cpu: 2 x Intel Xeon X5670, 12 cores, 24 threads
jaguaribe.why: Intel rates each 95 W, so 190 W for two at full tilt; a 2010 server's CPUs idle near 30 W each. The rest: a Supermicro X8DTL's 5500 chipset (27 W alone), 48 GB of DDR3 ECC, disks and server fans. No sensor: Westmere has no energy counter.

bosporus.cpu: 2 x Intel Xeon E5645, 12 cores, 24 threads
bosporus.why: Intel rates each 80 W, so 160 W for two; the rest as jaguaribe's, a dual-socket server of the same age with six DIMMs. No sensor.

macmini.why: Apple publishes the Mac mini M4 at the wall: about 4 W idle, 65 W at its most with CPU and GPU both loaded; the CPU alone near 38 W. Its figures include its own supply, so no efficiency is applied.

mac.why: Apple publishes the 24-inch iMac (M1) at the wall: about 10 W idle with its display on, and about 85 W at its most, display bright and GPU loaded; its eight CPU cores near 28 W all busy. Its lane is held to 2 CPUs of 8 at the background policy, so a job of it is a quarter of its cores. Estimates: no counter a user may read.

orchestrator.about: Orrery itself on the Mac: the console, the keeper, the planner's passes, the chores and the keeper's ssh. A planner pass is one core while it runs; the rest is measured from ps each five minutes (steady_cores until six samples say).
